themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis Erupts
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 3 this week—a 1,100% jump from the 8-week average of 0.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting either a new noise source, event pattern, or enforcement gap at a specific park in Tottenville/Great Kills that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Highest statistical anomaly in district 311 data this week
No Reddit or local news coverage yet—ground-level story opportunity
reporting_angles: Identify which park(s) are generating complaints and interview residents about source and timing
Contact Parks Dept. to determine if new event, equipment malfunction, or enforcement lapse is responsible

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped to 36 this week—a 67% spike from the 8-week average of 21.5 complaints (z-score: 5.21)—affecting households across the district and indicating a potential widespread disturbance pattern or seasonal change worth documenting.
evidence: 36 residential noise complaints this week vs. 21.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (67% spike, z-score: 5.21)
Second-highest spike in district this week by statistical significance
Residential noise in top 10 complaint types over 90 days (353 total), indicating baseline frustration
reporting_angles: Survey multiple residents to identify common complaint sources (construction, bars, vehicles, neighbors)
Check if spike correlates with any new business openings, demolition permits, or weekend event schedule

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints surged to 24 last week—a 269% jump from the 8-week average of 6.5 complaints (z-score: 5.11)—while new tree requests spiked to 4 this week (1,500% above baseline at 0.2 avg, z-score: 5.67), together signaling acute tree canopy stress and unmet forestry needs that align with a long-standing community board budget request.
evidence: 24 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 6.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (269% spike, z-score: 5.11)
4 new tree requests this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,500% spike, z-score: 5.67)
Damaged Tree complaints in top 10 over 90 days (424 total); forestry services is repeated community board budget request (#01 priority, unsolved year-over-year)
reporting_angles: Investigate what is killing or stressing trees in district (disease, pests, infrastructure conflict, storm damage from recent weather)
Interview Parks Dept. about response timeline and connect to chronic underfunding flagged in community board budget requests

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints jumped to 13 last week—a 197% spike from the 8-week average of 4.4 complaints (z-score: 5.22)—suggesting deteriorating public infrastructure or facilities that may affect parks, schools, libraries, or other district assets.
evidence: 13 maintenance or facility complaints last week vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (197% spike, z-score: 5.22)
Fourth-highest spike in district by statistical significance last week
Category is broad; requires granular 311 data to pinpoint affected facilities (parks, schools, etc.)
reporting_angles: Request detailed 311 complaint logs to identify which specific facilities or infrastructure are failing
Cross-reference with Parks, DOE, NYPL, and other agency service requests to build narrative

themes_detail.label: Police Non-Emergency Calls Elevated
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints spiked to 18 two weeks ago—a 157% jump from the 8-week average of 7.0 complaints (z-score: 4.8)—indicating elevated low-level public safety concerns or quality-of-life issues that may warrant NYPD attention (the district has long sought a new precinct facility per community board requests).
evidence: 18 non-emergency police matter complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (157% spike, z-score: 4.8)
Community board has repeatedly requested new NYPD facility (precinct house or sub-precinct, #01 budget priority)
No constituent services or Reddit data available to corroborate or specify complaint nature
reporting_angles: Obtain granular 311 data to identify what non-emergency police matters are being reported (disorderly conduct, trespassing, loitering, etc.)
Interview residents and NYPD to assess whether spike reflects actual increase in incidents or under-policing perception
